title: efference user configuration
description:
Settings for every session on this machine: connections to model providers, role
defaults, the web interface, how the terminal UI draws, where efference keeps the
secrets it writes, and whether it checks for newer versions. It names where each
credential comes from, never the credential itself. `efference setup` writes it, and
a host reads it when it starts.

connections.description:
Connections to model providers, by name. A session names its model as
`<connection>/<model>`, as in `"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5"`.

env_hook.description:
A program and its arguments whose output is a session's starting environment, as
in `["/bin/zsh", "-l", "-c", "env -0"]`. It runs directly, without a shell, in the
session's project directory, and must print NUL-separated `KEY=value` records
(what `env -0` writes); they replace the host's environment rather than adding to
it. Omitted, sessions inherit the host's environment.

Auth.description:
Where the connection's credential comes from, by `kind`; never the credential
itself. Required with `provider`. On a described endpoint it may be omitted, and
then no credential is sent.

oneOf.description:
`{ kind = "env", key = "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" }`: an environment variable in the
host's environment.

key.description: The environment variable that holds the credential.

oneOf.description: `{ kind = "codex-cache" }`: the Codex CLI's ChatGPT login. For `openai-codex`.

`{ kind = "oauth" }`: a ChatGPT login made in `efference setup`, which keeps it in
the OS secret store and refreshes it. For `openai-codex`.

name.description: The login's name in the secret store. Default: the connection's name.

oneOf.description:
`{ kind = "keychain" }`: a key in the OS secret store, which `efference setup`
fills when a key is pasted.

name.description: The key's name in the secret store. Default: the connection's name.

Connection.description:
A connection to a model provider: a `provider` efference knows by name, or a
`dialect` and `base-url` describing another endpoint.

base-url.description:
The endpoint's base URL, as in `https://api.example.com/v1`. Required with
`dialect`; refused with `provider`, which has its own.

dialect.description:
The wire format of an endpoint efference has no name for. Requires `base-url`;
takes no `provider`.

enumValues: TypeSafe's System One decision models, which can serve as the spotter only.

disabled.description:
Keep the connection written down without offering it to any session. Default
`false`.

output-cap-field.description:
The request field that carries the output cap. Read on a `completions` connection
only. Default `"max_tokens"`.

enumValues: The default, which most servers read.

provider.description:
A provider efference knows by name, which sets the endpoint, the credential's
shape, and the wire format. Takes no `dialect` or `base-url`.

enumValues: The Codex backend, billed to a ChatGPT subscription.
TypeSafe's decision models, which can serve as the spotter only.

spotter-model.description:
The spotter model for sessions whose main model is on this connection, when
neither the session nor `[defaults].spotter` names one.

Defaults.description: `[defaults]`: role choices for sessions that make none.

spotter.description:
The spotter model, as `<connection>/<model>`, for sessions that name none. Unset, a
session uses its main connection's `spotter-model`, then the provider's default.

Host.description:
`[host]`: where a host started with `efference --host` serves the web interface.
With no `bind` it serves only its Unix socket. A flag beside `efference --host`
overrides each key for that launch.

bind.description:
`ADDR:PORT` for the web interface's TCP listener, as in `"127.0.0.1:7878"`. Plain
HTTP is refused on any address but loopback, so another address needs `tls-cert`
and `tls-key`.

public-url.description:
The address browsers open, `https://name[:port]`: the link the host prints, and
the only Host a request may name. Required with TLS; on a loopback bind it
defaults to `http://localhost:<port>`.

tls-cert.description:
The PEM certificate chain the bind serves, such as `tailscale cert` writes. A
leading `~/` is your home directory.

tls-key.description: The PEM private key matching `tls-cert`. A leading `~/` is your home directory.

ImageMode.description: How the terminal UI draws images in tool results. Default `"auto"`.

enumValues:
Ask the terminal which graphics protocol it supports, and fall back to half-block
characters when nothing answers.

Use the kitty graphics protocol, for a kitty terminal that tmux hides from
detection.
Use iTerm2's inline image protocol, for a terminal detection missed.
Show each image as a one-line reference.

Secrets.description:
`[secrets]`: keep the secrets efference writes (sign-ins, the web interface's root
secret, keys pasted into setup) with commands you name instead of the OS keychain,
as on a server with no Secret Service. With the table present the keychain is never
opened. `{name}` in an argument is replaced by the item's name, such as
`oauth:codex` or `root`; a value travels on stdin and stdout, never in an argument.
Any program running as you can run the same `get`.

absent_status.description:
The exit status `get` gives for an item that does not exist, such as `254` for
`aws ssm` or `1` for `secret-tool`; `delete` exiting with it is a success too.
Unset, every failure of `get` is an error, including the first read of an item
efference has not stored yet.

delete.description:
The program and arguments that remove an item. Optional: without it, an
operation that removes one (an MCP server's `--reauth`, a connection renamed in
`efference setup`) fails, naming the item to remove by hand.

get.description:
The program and arguments that print an item's value on stdout, as in
`["pass", "show", "efference/{name}"]`. One trailing newline is trimmed. It runs
directly, without a shell.

set.description:
The program and arguments that store an item, replacing any previous value. The
value arrives on stdin, with no newline added, as in
`["pass", "insert", "--multiline", "--force", "efference/{name}"]`.

Tui.description: `[tui]`: how the terminal UI draws. Read by each terminal client, not by the host.

frame-cost.description:
Time each paint and print the distribution on exit. Development instrumentation
for the streaming render.

theme.description:
The color theme: a built-in name such as `"Catppuccin Frappe"`, `"Nord"`, or
`"gruvbox-dark"`, or the path to a `.tmTheme` file. An unknown name lists the
built-in ones at launch, and a leading `~/` in a path is your home directory.
Default `"Catppuccin Frappe"`.

Updates.description: `[updates]`: whether efference checks for newer versions of itself.

check.description:
Ask efference.net when a host starts, and about once a day after, whether a
newer version of efference is out, and say so in the terminal UI and web
client. Nothing is installed. `efference setup` asks and writes the answer;
with no answer, nothing is asked. `efference update --check` asks once either
way.
